title: Understanding Database Connection Pooling Trade-offs
explanation: Database connection pooling reduces the overhead of establishing TCP connections for every incoming request. By maintaining a reusable pool of active sockets, applications decrease latency and conserve database memory. However, setting the pool size too high exhausts database resources and causes thread contention. Setting it too low creates queuing bottlenecks during traffic spikes. Developers must tune pool sizes based on available CPU cores and actual query execution time. Proper monitoring prevents silent failures under heavy load.
takeaway: Size your connection pools based on actual database concurrency limits rather than application thread counts to prevent resource exhaustion.
author: Muhammad Junaeid
